virginia-state-capitol.name: Virginia State Capitol
virginia-state-capitol.description: Neoclassical capitol building designed with Thomas Jefferson's input, completed in 1788; still houses the Virginia General Assembly.

main-street-station.name: Main Street Station
main-street-station.description: 1901 French Renaissance Revival railway station with a distinctive clock tower, in Shockoe Bottom; still an active Amtrak stop.

the-jefferson-hotel.name: The Jefferson Hotel
the-jefferson-hotel.description: Opulent 1895 Beaux-Arts hotel designed by Carrère and Hastings, known for its grand staircase and rooftop palm court.

old-city-hall.name: Old City Hall
old-city-hall.description: High Victorian Gothic government building completed in 1894, adjacent to Capitol Square; now used as office space.

richmond-city-hall.name: Richmond City Hall
richmond-city-hall.description: Richmond's modern City Hall tower on East Broad Street, modeled from the city's public scene dimensions and its mapped tower footprint.

carpenter-theatre-dominion-energy-center.name: Carpenter Theatre / Dominion Energy Center
carpenter-theatre-dominion-energy-center.description: 1928 Loew's movie palace restored as the Carpenter Theatre, now the anchor venue of the Dominion Energy Center for the Performing Arts.

federal-reserve-bank-of-richmond.name: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond
federal-reserve-bank-of-richmond.description: Aluminum-clad Fifth District Federal Reserve headquarters tower designed by Minoru Yamasaki, built 1975-1978 overlooking the James River.

james-monroe-building.name: James Monroe Building
james-monroe-building.description: State office tower on Capitol Square housing several Virginia state agencies, named for President James Monroe.

dominion-energy-tower-600-canal-place.name: Dominion Energy tower (600 Canal Place)
dominion-energy-tower-600-canal-place.description: High-rise corporate headquarters of Dominion Energy at 600 Canal Place, one of the tallest buildings in downtown Richmond's skyline.

altria-theater.name: Altria Theater
altria-theater.description: 1927 Shriners' Mosque-style auditorium later known as the Landmark Theater, now a major performing arts and concert venue near Monroe Park.

byrd-theatre.name: Byrd Theatre
byrd-theatre.description: Lavish 1928 movie palace on Cary Street with an original Wurlitzer organ, still operating as a single-screen cinema.

monument-avenue-streetscape.name: Monument Avenue streetscape
monument-avenue-streetscape.description: Grand tree-lined boulevard of Victorian and Beaux-Arts mansions with a landscaped median, a National Historic Landmark district.

hollywood-cemetery.name: Hollywood Cemetery
hollywood-cemetery.description: 1849 rural garden cemetery on the James River bluffs, burial site of two U.S. presidents and Confederate president Jefferson Davis.

belle-isle-footbridge.name: Belle Isle footbridge
belle-isle-footbridge.description: Pedestrian suspension footbridge beneath the Robert E. Lee Bridge connecting downtown to Belle Isle, a former factory site turned riverfront park.

foundry-park-south.name: Foundry Park South
foundry-park-south.description: The six-storey mass-timber amenity building at CoStar's Foundry Park campus, with dining, fitness, training and auditorium space plus ground-floor retail facing the riverfront.

costar-tower.name: CoStar Tower
costar-tower.description: CoStar Group's riverfront office tower at Foundry Park, connected to the firm's existing 501 South Fifth Street campus. Its glass facade, illuminated vertical crown and rooftop drone port reshape Richmond's skyline.

mayo-bridge.name: Mayo Bridge
mayo-bridge.description: Richmond's oldest James River highway crossing, carrying US 360; the current structure dates to 1913 on a river-crossing site used since colonial times.

canal-walk-tredegar-iron-works.name: Canal Walk + Tredegar Iron Works
canal-walk-tredegar-iron-works.description: Riverfront walkway along the historic James River and Kanawha Canal, passing the ruins of the Tredegar Iron Works, a Confederate munitions foundry now home to the American Civil War Museum.

the-diamond.name: The Diamond
the-diamond.description: 1985 baseball stadium on North Arthur Ashe Boulevard, longtime home of the Richmond Flying Squirrels, now succeeded by a new ballpark under the CarMax Park name.

vcu-cabell-library.name: VCU Cabell Library
vcu-cabell-library.description: Main library of Virginia Commonwealth University's Monroe Park campus, named for novelist James Branch Cabell.

virginia-museum-of-fine-arts.name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
virginia-museum-of-fine-arts.description: State art museum campus on Arthur Ashe Boulevard, represented with measured multi-height wings and roof setbacks from the 2025 Richmond LiDAR.

maggie-l-walker-memorial.name: Maggie L. Walker memorial
maggie-l-walker-memorial.description: Bronze statue of banker and civic leader Maggie L. Walker by sculptor Toby Mendez, dedicated 2017 at Broad and Adams streets in Jackson Ward.

byrd-park-pump-house.name: Byrd Park Pump House
byrd-park-pump-house.description: 1883 Gothic Revival waterworks in grey granite by city engineer Wilfred Cutshaw, beside the James River and Kanawha Canal; its roof storey held an open-air dance hall. Listed on the National Register.

virginia-war-memorial-carillon.name: Virginia War Memorial Carillon
virginia-war-memorial-carillon.description: 240-foot brick bell tower with limestone trim by Cram & Ferguson, dedicated in 1932 as Virginia's memorial to the dead of the First World War. Its 53 bells still ring for concerts in Byrd Park.

cookie-factory-lofts.name: Cookie Factory Lofts
cookie-factory-lofts.description: 1927 reinforced-concrete factory for the Southern Biscuit Company (later Interbake Foods, maker of FFV cookies and crackers), converted to apartments in 2014. Its rooftop water tower and neon "Home of FFV Cookies and Crackers" sign are a Midtown landmark. Listed on the National Register.

science-museum-of-virginia.name: Science Museum of Virginia
science-museum-of-virginia.description: John Russell Pope's 1919 Broad Street Station, a limestone Beaux-Arts rail terminal with a domed rotunda and Doric portico on West Broad Street, home of the Science Museum of Virginia and its Dome theatre since 1977.

cathedral-of-the-sacred-heart.name: Cathedral of the Sacred Heart
cathedral-of-the-sacred-heart.description: Italian Renaissance Revival cathedral of the Catholic Diocese of Richmond (1906, Joseph H. McGinnis): a limestone Latin cross with a copper-domed crossing and a twin-towered portico facing Monroe Park.

st-pauls-episcopal-church.name: St. Paul's Episcopal Church
st-pauls-episcopal-church.description: Greek Revival church (1845, Thomas S. Stewart) on East Grace Street facing Capitol Square, with a Corinthian portico and tiered steeple; known as the "Cathedral of the Confederacy".

egyptian-building.name: Egyptian Building
egyptian-building.description: 1845 Egyptian Revival home of the Medical College of Virginia (Thomas S. Stewart), now VCU: battered stucco walls, a cavetto cornice and a columned portico on College Street.

riverfront-plaza-west-tower.name: Riverfront Plaza West Tower
riverfront-plaza-west-tower.description: The 901 East Byrd Street half of Riverfront Plaza (1990), twin notched-corner office towers on the James River that anchor the downtown skyline.

riverfront-plaza-east-tower.name: Riverfront Plaza East Tower
riverfront-plaza-east-tower.description: The 951 East Byrd Street half of Riverfront Plaza (1990), twin notched-corner office towers on the James River that anchor the downtown skyline.

hippodrome-theater.name: Hippodrome Theater
hippodrome-theater.description: 1914 vaudeville and movie house on North 2nd Street, the heart of Jackson Ward's "Harlem of the South", restored in 2011 with its marquee and vertical sign.

childrens-hospital-of-richmond-at-vcu.name: Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU
childrens-hospital-of-richmond-at-vcu.matched: override:Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU
childrens-hospital-of-richmond-at-vcu.description: The Children's Tower (2023) of the Children's Hospital of Richmond at VCU on East Broad Street: a glass inpatient tower rising from a broad podium, Virginia's largest dedicated pediatric hospital building.

truist-place.name: Truist Place
truist-place.description: 400 ft office tower between East Main and East Cary Streets (formerly SunTrust Center), one of the tallest buildings on the downtown skyline, with a lower wing stepping up the slope toward 10th Street.

virginia-war-memorial.name: Virginia War Memorial
virginia-war-memorial.description: Virginia's memorial to its war dead on the bluff above the James: the 1956 Shrine of Memory, an open marble-and-glass pavilion engraved with nearly 12,000 names around the 23 ft Memory statue, with the Education Center and the Heilman Amphitheatre beside it.

american-civil-war-museum.name: American Civil War Museum
american-civil-war-museum.description: Brick and glass museum (3North, 2019) at Historic Tredegar, set into Gambles Hill between the old gun foundry and the Pattern Building, whose glass lobby encloses a surviving ruin wall of the Tredegar Iron Works.
